flaw.ctx: You asked for an LRU cache. It passes put-then-get.
flaw.answer: **Get never moves the node to the front**, so reads do not count as use. Put 1, put 2, get 1, put 3 → key 1 (just read) is evicted. Passes put/get tests; fails the first eviction-after-read test.
flaw.fix: Move the node to the front in Get, exactly as Put does.

qa.a: O(1) average for lookup, insert, remove; O(n) worst case if many keys collide. Enumeration is O(n) and order is not guaranteed.

Separate chaining, but without node objects: an `int[] buckets` of indices into an `Entry[]` array, each entry carrying its hash, key, value and a `next` index. Colliding keys form a chain through `next`.

When the entries array is full it grows to a larger prime (about double) and every entry is rehashed into new buckets — O(n) for that insert, amortised O(1). Pre-size with the constructor capacity when you know n.
Removing does not shrink anything: freed slots go on a free list for reuse. `TrimExcess()` shrinks. A struct key that is large is copied into every entry.
Red-black tree: O(log n) insert, remove, lookup; in-order enumeration.

qa.q: How do you get a floor (largest ≤ x)?
qa.a: `GetViewBetween(min, x).Max` — O(log n). There is no `floorKey` like Java's TreeMap.
O(1) `Remove(node)`, `AddFirst`, `RemoveLast` given a `LinkedListNode<T>` handle. Storing the handle in the dictionary avoids an O(n) search.
No. Concurrent `Remove`/`AddFirst` corrupts its pointers (R3 corrupted in 20/20 runs).

Only code that locks the *same object*. `lock (x)` is `Monitor.Enter/Exit` on x's object header, in a try/finally. It also acts as a full memory barrier, so writes inside are visible to the next locker.
Yes, with two locks taken in different orders (D5), or with a call out to unknown code while holding the lock. One lock and no callouts cannot deadlock. `Monitor` is re-entrant for the same thread.

Uncontended, a lock is tens of nanoseconds. Contended, threads spin briefly then block, causing context switches; throughput collapses toward one thread's worth. The fix is less work under the lock, or more locks (striping).
`this`, a `Type`, a string — other code can lock them too. Use a private readonly object (or `System.Threading.Lock` in .NET 9+).

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: A cache that evicts the least frequently used key, breaking ties by least recently used, with `GetRank(key)`: the key's position in keep-order.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Get and Put as close to O(1) as rank allows — state the cost
- Evict min frequency; among equals, least recent
- `GetRank(key)`: 1 = safest, Count = next victim; −1 if absent
- GetRank is a read of metadata — it must not change frequency (say this; the statement does not)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: O(1) LFU needs one linked list *per frequency* and a `minFreq` pointer: a touch moves a node from list f to list f+1. **Rank cannot be O(1) with that structure** — it needs to know how many keys sit above you. A sorted count per frequency gives O(distinct frequencies + bucket size). Say that before the assistant claims O(1).

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: `byKey: key → node`, `buckets: freq → LinkedList`, `freqCounts: SortedDictionary<freq, count>`, `minFreq`. Empty buckets are deleted, not left behind.

learn.title: 5 · Why the approach works
learn.md:
- Touch: detach from bucket f; if that bucket emptied and f was min, min = f+1; attach to bucket f+1 at the front.
- Put new: if full, evict `buckets[minFreq].Last`; insert at freq 1; minFreq = 1.
- GetRank: 1 + Σ counts of frequencies above f + position of the node from the front of its bucket.

learn.title: 6 · Data structures
learn.md:
| Type | Why |
|---|---|
| Dictionary<int, LinkedList<Entry>> | One recency list per frequency; First = most recent |
| SortedDictionary<int,int> | Ordered counts per frequency, for rank |
| int _minFreq | The eviction bucket, in O(1); reset to 1 on every insert |

learn.title: 7 · C# implementation — walkthrough
learn.md:
- Touch: detach from bucket f; if that bucket emptied and f was min, min = f+1; attach to bucket f+1 at the front.
- Put new: if full, evict `buckets[minFreq].Last`; insert at freq 1; minFreq = 1.
- GetRank: 1 + Σ counts of frequencies above f + position of the node from the front of its bucket.

learn.title: 8 · Complexity
learn.md: Get/Put O(log F), not O(1): the sorted count map that GetRank needs costs a log per touch (F = distinct frequencies, small in practice). Drop it and Get/Put are O(1) — that is the price of rank, and saying so is the point. GetRank O(F + B); an order-statistics tree makes it O(log n).

learn.title: 9 · Edge cases
learn.md:
- a touched twice, b once, c never → ranks 1, 2, 3.
- GetRank does not change rank (call it twice).
- Tie at freq 1: the more recent key ranks higher; the older one is evicted.
- Capacity one under churn: minFreq resets correctly after evicting a high-frequency key.
- Missing key → −1.

learn.title: 10 · Tests
learn.md:
**S1 — LFU with LRU tie-break**

- least frequent (c) evicted
- a and b survive
- tie broken by recency: 1 evicted
- capacity 1 churn: minFreq resets

**S2 — GetRank**

- a rank 1
- b rank 2
- c rank 3 = next victim
- GetRank is not a use
- missing key
- equal frequency: more recent ranks higher

learn.title: 11 · AI usage strategy
learn.md:
- Give it your fields and ask for Touch only — that is where the minFreq bug lives.
- Ask: "What is the complexity of GetRank as written? Do not claim O(1) unless every step is O(1)."

**Prompts for this question:**

- *Check my design — no code* — "I believe one recency list per frequency plus a minFreq pointer gives O(1) LFU with LRU tie-breaking, and rank cannot also be O(1) with that structure. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?"
- *Review, do not rewrite* — "Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it."
- *Race conditions* — "Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call TryGet, Put and GetRank concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet."
- *Tests that expose bugs* — "Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct."
- *Complexity check* — "What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it."
- *Requirement change* — "The requirement changed: Add int GetRank(TKey key): rank 1 is the entry evicted last (highest frequency, most recent among equals); rank Count is the next victim; -1 if absent. GetRank must not count as a use. List which members need to change and which do not, before writing any code."

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Claiming O(1) GetRank.
- Forgetting to reset minFreq to 1 on insert.
- Leaving empty buckets in the map, so minFreq advances past them incorrectly.
- GetRank calling Touch — reading the rank changes it.

**Verification exercise:** Bug — **Get never moves the node to the front**, so reads do not count as use. Put 1, put 2, get 1, put 3 → key 1 (just read) is evicted. Passes put/get tests; fails the first eviction-after-read test.

learn.title: 13 · Concurrency considerations
learn.md:
A touch updates four things (two buckets, the counts, minFreq). Any partial view breaks eviction. One lock; no reader/writer lock, because Get writes.

**Level 3 — Concurrency**

- *Thread-safety — reader/writer lock?* — One lock; Get writes, so RW does not help

learn.title: 14 · Scalability considerations
learn.md:
**Level 4 — Scale**

- *Millions of keys; frequencies grow forever.* — Aging (halve periodically) or W-TinyLFU

learn.title: 15 · Production considerations
learn.md:
- Frequency aging, or the cache fossilises around yesterday's hot keys.
- Rank is a debugging/observability feature — say how often it is called before optimising it.

**Level 5 — Productionisation**

- *How would you know the cache has fossilised?* — Age of evicted entries, hit ratio on new keys

learn.title: 16 · Follow-up questions
learn.md:
- *Implement LFU.* — Buckets + minFreq. State the tie-break.
- *Add GetRank.* — Define rank first. Then admit the complexity honestly.
- *Make GetRank O(log n).* — Fenwick tree indexed by frequency for the "above me" count; within-bucket position still needs an order-statistic per bucket, or a global order-statistics tree keyed (freq, lastUse).
- *Thread-safe.* — One lock — every operation touches several structures. Rank reads also need the lock.
- *Old popular keys never leave.* — LFU's known flaw. Age frequencies (halve them periodically) or use W-TinyLFU.

**Level 1 — Correctness**

- *GetRank on a missing key? Ties at the minimum frequency?* — −1; least recent loses

**Level 2 — Complexity**

- *Complexity of GetRank — and of Get/Put given the sorted counts?* — O(F + B); O(log F)
- *Can GetRank be O(log n)?* — Order-statistics / Fenwick

stages.name: LFU with LRU tie-break
stages.yours: Fields: `Dictionary<TKey, Entry>`, `Dictionary<int, LinkedList<Entry>>` buckets by frequency (most recent first), and `_minFreq`. Rules: evict the **back of bucket[_minFreq]**; a use moves an entry from f to f+1; **a new key resets _minFreq to 1**.
stages.ai: **Co-generate.** The O(1) design is in your fields; what remains is bookkeeping.
bad: Either eviction by **scanning for the minimum frequency** (O(n)), or a SortedDictionary (O(log n)) — described as O(1). Tie-break by recency often missing.
No complexity target, so it picks whatever is easiest
The tie-break rule is not stated, so it is guessed
The O(1) claim is not true — and it will say it is
good: Implement TryGet and Put in LfuRankCache below in O(1): my entries map, frequency buckets (LinkedList, most recent at the front) and _minFreq. A use moves an entry from bucket f to f+1; if bucket f empties and f was _minFreq, _minFreq becomes f+1. When full, evict the back of bucket[_minFreq]. A new key starts at frequency 1 and sets _minFreq = 1. Keep my fields. Assumptions first. No SortedDictionary, no scan for the minimum. Show only TryGet, Put and their helpers.
Every invariant stated — especially the **_minFreq** updates
Tie-break is built into "back of the bucket"
stages.reply: Typical defect: **_minFreq not reset to 1 on insert**. After churn it points at an empty bucket and the next eviction throws KeyNotFoundException.
validate: Capacity 1 churn: put, read twice, put, put — _minFreq must reset
Equal frequency: the least recently used goes
Put of an existing key is a use
No scan over entries in TryGet or Put
stages.fix: A missing `_minFreq = 1` is one line → **by hand**.
stages.say: "Eviction reads bucket[minFreq], so minFreq must be right after every operation — a new key always makes it 1."
stages.require: Implement `LfuRankCache<TKey,TValue>`: `TryGet`, `Put`, `Count`. A Put to an existing key counts as a use.
stages.say_iv: Implement an LFU cache: evict the least frequently used key, and break ties by least recently used.

stages.name: GetRank
stages.yours: **Decide the complexity and say it first.** A scan comparing (frequency, last use) is O(n) and fine to start; O(log n) needs an order-statistics tree. Rank 1 = evicted last. **GetRank is not a use.**
stages.ai: **Co-generate the simple version**, and make the AI state its complexity — then check that claim against the code.
bad: Add GetRank to the LFU cache in O(1).
A confident "O(1)" that walks the buckets (O(n)) — or one that calls TryGet to find the entry, so asking for a rank changes the ranking.
Demands a complexity that does not exist, so you get a false claim
Does not say GetRank is not a use
good: Add GetRank(key): 1 = the entry that would be evicted last, Count = the next victim, -1 if missing. Higher frequency ranks higher; equal frequency, more recently used ranks higher. It must not count as a use. O(n) is acceptable — state the complexity in a comment. Store a last-use counter on each entry if you need one. Keep my fields; do not use TryGet inside GetRank. Show only GetRank.
Honest complexity, stated in the code
stages.reply: Typical defect: **GetRank calls TryGet** to find the entry — a read that bumps the frequency. Ask twice and the answer changes.
validate: GetRank twice gives the same answer
Equal frequency: more recent ranks higher
Its complexity comment matches the code
stages.fix: TryGet inside GetRank → **by hand**: read the entries map directly.
stages.say: "GetRank is O(n) and I'd say so. If rank is hot, an order-statistics tree makes it O(log n) at the cost of O(log n) updates."
stages.require: Add `int GetRank(TKey key)`: rank 1 is the entry evicted last (highest frequency, most recent among equals); rank Count is the next victim; -1 if absent. GetRank must not count as a use.
stages.say_iv: Add GetRank(key): the key's position if entries were ordered by frequency. Tell me its complexity before you write it.
